mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25 percentage points over the next month, the S&P 500 forward 20-day return is expected to be negative due to higher real borrowing costs compressing equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the next month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the 30-day moving average during the trigger period (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in PAYEMS (employment growth) of at least 50,000 jobs is associated with a positive S&P 500 forward return over the next 60 trading days as labor market strength supports corporate optimism.
failure_condition: Over 60-day horizon, 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in HOUST (residential construction) of 10% or more predicts a negative S&P 500 forward return over the next 5 days as weak housing demand reduces corporate earnings expectations.
candidate_trigger: HOUST < (current value * 0.9) for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When INDPRO (industrial production) falls by 5% or more over the next quarter, the S&P 500 20-day forward return is expected to be negative due to supply-side weakness reducing corporate profit expectations.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < (current value * 0.95) over the next 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly worse than the 30-day rolling average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in UNRATE (unemployment rate) below 7% for two consecutive months creates a positive S&P 500 20-day forward return as lower labor costs boost corporate profitability.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the prior 20-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly increases in both GDPC1 (GDP) and RSAFS (retail sales) above their 12-month averages predict a positive S&P 500 60-day forward return as dual demand signals boost investor confidence.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 30-day moving average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When PAYEMS falls by 20,000 jobs in a month (indicating job market weakness), the S&P 500 20-day forward return turns negative due to reduced consumer spending and corporate risk aversion.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is not statistically lower than the prior 5-day average (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of accelerating CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 2%, the S&P 500 5-day forward return is expected to be negative as markets anticipate tighter policy and discount future earnings.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not statistically lower than the prior 3-day average (t-test p > 0.05).
